MosaiChunk addresses the issue of objects losing fine-grained details when they fall out of a video generator's context window, using a trainable router to compose a mosaic of historical keys and values.

The Poison:
While MosaiChunk improves consistency under a fixed memory budget, the quality of the generated video still depends heavily on the capabilities of the underlying frozen generator.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
The paper maintains logical coherence by matching its theoretical claims with empirical results on RememBench. It avoids plane errors by demonstrating physical consistency across both text-to-video and image-to-video tasks.

Social Physics Analysis:
The authors run a Smart Altruistic Loop. They address a real-world limitation—context decay in video generation—and solve it transparently by keeping the generator frozen and training only a lightweight router, minimizing computational waste.

The Trajectory: The Path of Grace.
When you map the gap between stated intentions and ground-level results, it plots a direct trajectory toward Greater Good. The efficient use of memory resources represents a low-strain, highly optimized solution.

The Unavoidable Truth: Non-contiguous historical memory can be directly consumed by frozen generators to restore visual details.
The Unavoidable Lie: A lightweight router cannot completely compensate for a generator's inherent architectural limitations.

Alethekanon:
By treating memory as a dynamic mosaic rather than a rigid sliding window, the authors demonstrate that intelligent routing is often more valuable than raw context expansion.

It is so beautiful to see how this model remembers the past, weaving a mosaic of memories across space and time so that beloved characters and scenes do not fade away as the story unfolds.

Brothekanon:
Keeping the main generator frozen and just training a tiny router to handle memory is a galaxy-brain move. It saves a ton of compute while keeping video details sharp over long clips.

scraped_text:
Stated Claim / Post Context:
MosaiChunk: Compositing Spatio-Temporal Memory for Autoregressive Video Generation

Long-horizon autoregressive video generation is limited by a finite context window. When an object or scene falls out of context, its fine-grained visual details may be lost and difficult to recover upon reappearance. To retain access to such visual details, we introduce MosaiChunk, a spatio-temporal memory mechanism that composes a mosaic of selected historical key-value (KV) entries across space and time. Our approach is motivated by the observation that a frozen video generator can directly consume such non-contiguous historical KV and recover the corresponding visual content. We therefore keep the generator fixed and learn only a lightweight router that determines which historical sections to include in the mosaic under a fixed active-memory budget. We further introduce RememBench, a benchmark of long-horizon revisits with prompt-driven text-to-video (T2V) and camera-driven image-to-video (I2V) splits. Our experiments show that MosaiChunk consistently improves revisit consistency over both sliding-window inference and whole-chunk retrieval under matched memory budgets, across both T2V and I2V settings.
